comments.body:
From what I recall, it's not trivial to move the constant back into the `poll_fn` scope because we are relying on the access in broader scope to initialize the non-biased rotator.

But, this is indeed clear semver breakage, sorry to introduce these hygiene concerns.

Perhaps a decent middle ground might be to just make the constant something that is very unlikely to collide with existing user declarations? For instance `TOKIO_TRY_JOIN_BRANCH_COUNT`?

I think we can use a very very looooooooong and unusual name for this `const COUNT: u32`, while this is still possible to collide, but very unlikely.

Another solution is storing an `u32` into the `Rotator`.

<del>I prefer the first one as it is the minimal change.</del>


I prefer the second one as the any collision might change the runtime behavior. What do you think @jlizen ?

I prefer the first option of an unlikely to collide name. 

Storing the count inside the rotator would increase the memory size of the future beyond its original (pre-biased feature) footprint since we still need access to the count inside the poll loop as well, resulting in the variable being stored in two places. The current implementation avoids this by using a const generic.

Avoiding additional memory footprint was a chief concern that drove the current implementation.

It seems like a better tradeoff for most users (or presumably all, if a weird enough variable name were picked) to optimize for memory footprint. This came up in this issue since we are instead using an extremely common variable name.

That said I'm open to going with option 2 (store in rotator) if that is the general preference though i'd suggest getting Alice's opinion as well as she guided the initial implementation.

> It seems like a better tradeoff for most users (or presumably all

That makes a lot of sense, and I get your point.

But I still think reliability matters more than performance—those very rare bugs can be really painful when they happen.

@Darksonn What do you think?

Edit: nvm, that won't work, since I still will need to manipulate the variable while preserving its original value. Really would need the const generic to avoid the memory increase. And my understanding is that declaring the const is all is what is breaking hygiene.

~~I could possibly finagle it to just bundle the counter used inside the poll function inside the rotator. That would trade a bit of complexity for no additional memory footprint. Let me poke around and see what I can do~~

~~Would you want a quickie PR to obfuscate the variable name in the meantime as a stopgap for this issue? Or hold out for the deeper fix?~~
Wouldn't that cause the same name collision, just now with a different type from the macro's constant?

Emm, it doesn't work. I thought this approach can at least report the type mismatch error instead of shadowing the variable secretly.

```
error: `PrivU32` is forbidden as the type of a const generic parameter
   --> tokio/src/macros/join.rs:231:33
    |
231 | pub struct Rotator<const COUNT: PrivU32> {
    |                                 ^^^^^^^
    |
    = note: the only supported types are integers, `bool`, and `char`

```

> How about something like this approach?

Good suggestion, thanks. I think that will work && address all concerns. Poking around with it now.
@robinhundt quick question: did linter report unsed variable for the shadowed `const COUNT: usize = 2 * DEFAULT_OT_BATCH_SIZE;`?

@ADD-SP in my case I directly got a compile error, as the types were different.
As [this playground](https://play.rust-lang.org/?version=stable&mode=debug&edition=2024&gist=aa3ca135a274e1029875470aa40b7518) shows, if the only use of the constant is within a macro where it is shadowed by another constant of the same name and type, you get an unused warning. However, if in the calling scope you have an actual use of the constant (like I did with my code with the `random_choices(COUNT)` line, which wasn't inside a join macro), you won't get this warning.
